newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Big tanker spill fouls Venezuelan waters.
newsitem.headline: Big tanker spill fouls Venezuelan waters.

text.p: A Greek tanker ran aground off western Venezuela spilling about 20,000 barrels of crude oil into the sea and threatening the shoreline, authorities said Sunday.

An oil slick about four miles (7 km) long formed in the Gulf of Venezuela, near San Carlos island, following the grounding late Friday night of the Nissos Amorgos, a spokesman for the state-run oil industry National Contingency Plan (PNC) said.
"It is estimated so far that about 20,000 barrels of crude were spilled in the Gulf of Venezuela," a PNC communique said.
"It could be one of the bigest oil spills ever in the area," PNC spokesman Pedro Marturano said earlier from Maracaibo, Venezuela's second city and capital of oil-rich Zulia state.

The tanker, which was carrying 474,000 barrels of crude from Lake Maracaibo to Italy, was towed nearer to shore and anchored 14 nautical miles (25 km) off Paraguana peninsula in Falcon state, on the eastern flank of the Gulf of Venezuela, the statement said.

Along the mangove-fringed western coast of the Gulf, experts using specialized equipment were working to contain the spill and scoop the oil. The extent of environmental damage was not immediately clear.
The tanker was chartered by Maraven, a subsidiary of state oil giant Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA).
